subject.title: fix(config): warn when JSON5 comments are lost on config write

question: Should ConfigWriteResult and ConfigReplaceResult permanently expose an optional comment-loss warning through the public plugin SDK, or should this diagnostic remain internal to OpenClaw's CLI/logging surface?
rationale: The issue is a valid data-loss bug, but the branch turns its mitigation into a new exported plugin contract; repository policy requires owner intent for that API direction, and automated review cannot choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Approve typed warning contract
options.body: Keep the optional warning fields, document their semantics, add focused SDK surface coverage, and require supported-command proof before merge.

options.title: Keep warning internal
options.body: Remove the exported result fields and retain only owner-controlled CLI or logger diagnostics, accepting that quiet callers receive no structured signal.

options.title: Pursue preservation instead
options.body: Pause this mitigation and implement a comment-preserving mutation path so supported config changes do not destroy authored JSON5 comments.

recommendation.title: Approve typed warning contract
recommendation.body: Keep the optional warning fields, document their semantics, add focused SDK surface coverage, and require supported-command proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows broad ownership of config write behavior and plugin runtime documentation, making this the strongest available product-contract routing candidate.
